fix_first: By 2026-11-16, before the build-up starts: get the launch page's mobile LCP from 3.4 s to 2.5 s or less (compress and resize the hero screenshot image), then rerun the check.

tasks: Announce the date on 2026-11-17 to the 412 people on the Class booking waitlist and in the newsletter; tell supporters the same day.

Publish build-up content on the top search topics (how to reduce no shows, appointment reminder text, salon booking app); write a page for 'class booking software', where the site sits at position 14.2.
Ask smallbiz-weekly.example, behind the biggest past moment, for a launch-week placement.
Brief the webinar partner from June and book a class-booking session for launch week.
Countdown emails to the waitlist on 2026-11-24 and 2026-12-01; launch email drafted by 2026-12-01.
Paid creative submitted by 2026-12-01 to leave time for ad review.
Run of show below: launch page update, the email to the newsletter and the waitlist, the in-app message for current customers, social posts.
Follow up with everyone who engaged; onboarding emails for new sign-ups; a recap post in week 1; a studio case study by week 3; retargeting of launch visitors.
Outreach to the borrowed channels again with the first results.

channel_plan.plan: The biggest lever: owned channels bring 70.0% of sessions, the list is warm (last send 8 days ago, 9,960 reachable), and 412 people joined the waitlist. Send the launch email to both, switch on an in-app message for current customers, and point every other link at the launch page.

Facebook has 2,850 followers, 26 posts and 140 shares in 90 days: post the demo there and link the launch page. Organic Social is 2.5% of sessions, so don't plan the launch around it. Instagram and LinkedIn Pages are connected but not read here.

Repeat what worked: the 2026-01-20 moment was a one-source burst from smallbiz-weekly.example (8.03x), worth asking for again; the 2026-06-16 webinar with webinar-partner.example brought 2.73x. Add studio and trainer communities and newsletters, and a co-hosted webinar in launch week.

With the $3,000 budget: about $600 in the two weeks before (promote the build-up content to studio owners to grow the waitlist), $1,500 in launch week (more budget on the Brand campaign, which loses 12% of brand searches to budget, and the best launch post), $900 over the next three weeks (retargeting launch visitors). Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads and TikTok Ads are connected; no call here measures audience sizes, so check the retargeting pool in each platform before the pre-launch spend.

launch_day_run_of_show.do: Systems check, publish the launch page update and the announcement post, switch on the in-app message, send the launch email to the newsletter and the waitlist.
Post on the Facebook Page and personal profiles; personal notes to the webinar partner and the waitlist studios who tested early; reply to every comment.
Keep replying, share studio quotes as they come in (with their yes). A second email only to waitlist people who opened and didn't click: the list is large (9,960).
Short progress post, public thanks, triage issues, plan day 2.

release_notes.text: Studios can cap each class at a set number of seats, so a class never overbooks. Until now, a popular class kept taking bookings after it filled, and someone was turned away at the door. From November 4, bookings stop when a class reaches the seat limit you choose. How to set it: 1. Open Classes. [Screenshot: the Classes list] 2. Choose a class. 3. Enter the seat limit under Capacity and save. [Screenshot: the Capacity field] Also new for classes: when someone cancels, the first person on the class waitlist gets the seat and a confirmation automatically. Who has it: Growth and Business plans, on the web and in the app. Help article: example.com/help/class-capacity/ Also in this release: Set a different reminder time for each service, such as 48 hours before a colour appointment and 2 hours before a haircut. Refund part of a deposit from the booking screen instead of all or nothing.

go_to_market_motion.decision: Mixed: self-serve for single locations, and a salesperson for chains worth more than $549 a month. Self-serve pays back in 4.7 months; a salesperson pays back in 10.7 months on the average won chain, just inside the 12-month target, so only deals above the sales line should reach sales.

inputs_measured.left_out_of_self_serve: LinkedIn 'Multi-location chains: demo request' ($4,800, 40 leads): it collects leads for sales, so it counts once, as the sales route's lead cost
inputs_measured.ratio_note: purchase events divided by sign_up events in the same 90 days: a ratio of event counts, not a cohort

routes.why: single locations reach value in the first session and the owner pays by card; payback 4.7 months against a 12-month target. Chains need setup and several sign-offs, so not them.
average won chain $618 a month is above the $549 sales line (payback 10.7 months); 3 of 11 won deals were below the line and lost money inside the target.
no partner in place and no partner share given; ask what share a salon-supply distributor would take
nobody can run one this year; revisit as a later supplement

second_route_trigger.rule: accounts above the sales line per month × win rate ≥ won deals per salesperson per month
second_route_trigger.meaning: met: the chain demand above the line can keep one salesperson busy, so keep the role; route chains below the line to self-serve with setup help

self_serve_for_small_deals_trigger.rule: more than a quarter of won deals fall below the sales line

chosen_route_needs.self_serve: public prices, monthly plans, card checkout, upgrade without talking to anyone; metrics: visit to sign-up, sign-up to first booking, first booking to paid, payback
chosen_route_needs.sales_for_chains: a demo request page for 2 or more locations, a price range from $549 a month, annual terms; metrics: meetings, pipeline, win rate, cycle length (median 34 days today), sales cost per deal

unknowns: true cohort sign-up to paid (only event counts are available)

gates_fails_first.numbers: the insert card offers a free strap for a 5-star review: that is a reward conditioned on a positive review, banned by Amazon and by the FTC rule (16 CFR Part 465)
title 114 characters, no word more than twice; 5 bullets; backend terms 102 bytes
main image on pure white, plus in-use, size and detail images
profit before ads at the 15% coupon price $29.74: $10.16
75 days of cover against 49 days until the next shipment is live + 14 = 63

keep: Enrol units in Vine (Brand Registry is in place)
Use Request a Review within the window Seller Central allows after delivery

replace.was: Insert card: get a strap for free when you leave a 5-star review
replace.with: a neutral insert that asks for an honest review and offers help with any problem, with no reward

reviews_plan.never: paid, refunded, gifted or swapped reviews, reviews from staff, family or friends, asking only happy buyers; the Early Reviewer Program closed in 2021

phases.work: fix the two failing gates first (reviews plan, Attribution tags); stock checked in; Vine units ready; Sponsored Products built and paused

ads run to the 41.8% break-even ACOS from day 1 (no launch loss was accepted); automatic campaign plus an exact-match campaign on the 5 ranking keywords; the 15% coupon; Vine units go out; the brand's email list and social point at the listing through Attribution links
move converting search terms into exact match and add them as negatives in the automatic campaign; check indexing for each ranking keyword; check deal eligibility in Seller Central
bring ACOS to the 29.8% target; add Sponsored Brands; pause any keyword that spent more than $29.24 (two units' profit before ads) without a sale
TACOS falling week by week; reorder by the stock cover rule; plan a bundle or a second colour
